arxiv-2205-09286.title: Tighter sum uncertainty relations via metric-adjusted skew information
arxiv-2205-09286.creator: Hui Li, Ting Gao, Fengli Yan
arxiv-2205-09286.description: Abstract In this paper, we first provide three general norm inequalities, which are used to give new uncertainty relations of any finite observables and quantum channels via metric-adjusted skew information. The results are applicable to its special cases as Wigner-Yanase-Dyson skew information.

arxiv-2211-16168.title: Robust boundary integral equations for the solution of elastic scattering problems via Helmholtz decompositions
arxiv-2211-16168.creator: Víctor Domínguez, Catalin Turc
arxiv-2211-16168.description: Abstract Helmholtz decompositions of the elastic fields open up new avenues for the solution of linear elastic scattering problems via boundary integral equations (BIE) [Dong et al., Mathematics of Computation 90 (2021)]. The main appeal of this approach is that the ensuing systems of BIE feature only integral operators associated with the Helmholtz equation.

arxiv-2212-14846.title: Detection possibility of a Pseudo-FIMP in presence of a thermal WIMP
arxiv-2212-14846.creator: Subhaditya Bhattacharya, Jayita Lahiri, Dipankar Pradhan
arxiv-2212-14846.description: Abstract A dark matter (DM) having feeble interaction with the visible sector can thermalise via substantial interaction with a Weakly Interacting Massive Particle (WIMP). Such DM candidates are categorised as pseudo-FIMP (pFIMP). pFIMP can provide both direct and indirect search prospects via WIMP loop. This work focuses into such possibilities.

arxiv-2304-04807.title: Deep-learning based measurement of planetary radial velocities in the presence of stellar variability
arxiv-2304-04807.creator: Ian Colwell, Virisha Timmaraju, Hamsa Shwetha Venkataram, Alexander Wise
arxiv-2304-04807.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Ian Colwell, Virisha Timmaraju, Hamsa Shwetha Venkataram, Alexander Wise. We present a deep-learning based approach for measuring small planetary radial velocities in the presence of stellar variability. We use neural networks to reduce stellar RV jitter in three years of HARPS-N sun-as-a-star spectra. We develop and compare dimensionality-reduction and data splitting methods, as well as various neural network architectures including single line CNNs, an ensemble of single line CNNs, and a multi-line CNN.

arxiv-2403-05642.title: Stability of hypermassive neutron stars with realistic rotation and entropy profiles
arxiv-2403-05642.creator: Nishad Muhammed, Matthew D. Duez, Pavan Chawhan, Noora Ghadiri, Luisa T. Buchman, Francois Foucart, Patrick Chi-Kit Cheong, Lawrence E. Kidder, Harald P. Pfeiffer, Mark A. Scheel
arxiv-2403-05642.description: Abstract Binary neutron star mergers produce massive, hot, rapidly differentially rotating neutron star remnants; electromagnetic and gravitational wave signals associated with the subsequent evolution depend on the stability of these remnants. Stability of relativistic stars has previously been studied for uniform rotation and for a class of differential rotation with monotonic angular velocity profiles.

arxiv-2403-19337.title: The Hierarchical Cosmic Web and Assembly Bias
arxiv-2403-19337.creator: and D. Forero Sánchez
arxiv-2403-19337.description: Abstract Accurate modeling of galaxy distributions is paramount for cosmological analysis using galaxy redshift surveys. However, this endeavor is often hindered by the computational complexity of resolving the dark matter halos that host these galaxies. arxiv-2407-02108.title: Numerical Simulation of Polarized Light and Temperature with a Refractive Interface
arxiv-2407-02108.creator: Olivier Pironneau
arxiv-2407-02108.description: Abstract In this article we propose a numerical algorithm to compute the intensity and polarization of a polychromatic electromagnetic radiation crossing a medium with graded refractive index and modeled by the Vector Radiative Refractive Transfer Equations (VRRTE). Special attention is given to the case where the refractive index has a discontinuity for which the Fresnel conditions are necessary.

arxiv-2501-18434.creator: J. Zs. Mezei 1,2, A. Orbán 1, S. Demes 1, M. Ayouz 3,4, A. Faure 5, P. Hily-Blant 5, Ioan F. Schneider 2,6

arxiv-2508-17540.title: Activation Transport Operators
arxiv-2508-17540.creator: Andrzej Szablewski, Marek Masiak
arxiv-2508-17540.description: Abstract The residual stream mediates communication between transformer decoder layers via linear reads and writes of non-linear computations. While sparse-dictionary learning-based methods locate features in the residual stream, and activation patching methods discover circuits within the model, the mechanism by which features flow through the residual stream remains understudied.

pmc-10715115.title: Molecular Serotyping and Antibiotic Resistance Profile of Group B Streptococcus Strains Isolated from Iranian Pregnant Women with Urinary Tract Infection
pmc-10715115.creator: Natalie Gharabeigi, Akram Sadat Tabatabaee Bafroee, Kumarss Amini
pmc-10715115.description: Background: Group B Streptococcus (GBS) can cause serious infections in neonates and pregnant women. GBS may cause urinary tract infections (UTIs). However, molecular epidemiology of such infections is rarely reported. The present study aimed to determine drug resistance patterns and molecular serotyping of GBS isolates in a population of pregnant Iranian women with UTIs.

pmc-11449312.title: Impacts of resident physician unionization on house staff compensation
pmc-11449312.creator: Sidharth Tyagi, Rema J. Shah, Joshua Huttler, Jehanzeb Kayani, Mohammad-Reza Ghovanloo, Philip R. Effraim
pmc-11449312.description: BackgroundPhysicians-in-training in the United States work long hours for relatively low wages. In response to increased economic burden, the popularity of unionization in residency training programs has increased dramatically. In this study, we conducted a cross-sectional investigation of the association between unionization status and Internal Medicine PGY-1 compensation and benefits.

pmc-11656707.title: Direct Monomer Recovery from Ring-Closing Depolymerization of Thermosets
pmc-11656707.creator: Chihui Zheng, Gadi Slor, Youwei Ma, Francesco Stellacci
pmc-11656707.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Recovering monomers from the depolymerization of thermosets presents a significant challenge, which becomes even more daunting if one sets the goal of doing it directly, i.e., without complex chemical separation steps. To this end, we have synthesized a new type of polycarbonate thermoset by first copolymerizing alkyl cyclic carbonates (ACCs) with small amounts of allyloxy cyclic carbonates (AoCCs), followed by cross-linking the resulting allyloxy polycarbonate with excess tetrathiol compounds under UV irradiation.

pmc-12468325.title: Conformational and Functional Properties of the Bioactive Thiosemicarbazone and Thiocarbohydrazone Compounds
pmc-12468325.creator: Nikitas Georgiou, Ektoras Vasileios Apostolou, Stamatia Vassiliou, Demeter Tzeli, Thomas Mavromoustakos, Hidayat Hussain
pmc-12468325.description: Thiosemicarbazones and thiocarbohydrazones are key sulfur-containing organic compounds known for their diverse biological, pharmaceutical, and industrial applications. Beyond their well-established therapeutic potential, their strong chelating ability allows them to form stable complexes with transition metals, enabling uses in catalysis, corrosion inhibition, and dyeing processes.

pmc-12520519.title: RESP2: An Uncertainty Aware Multi‐Target Multi‐Property Optimization AI Pipeline for Antibody Discovery
pmc-12520519.creator: Jonathan Parkinson, Ryan Hard, Young Su Ko, Wei Wang
pmc-12520519.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Discovery of therapeutic antibodies against infectious disease pathogens presents distinct challenges. Ideal candidates must possess not only the properties required for any therapeutic antibody (e.g., specificity, low immunogenicity) but also high affinity to many mutants of the target antigen. Here, we present RESP2, an enhanced version of the Rapid Engineering System for Proteins (RESP) pipeline, designed for the discovery of antibodies against one or multiple antigens with simultaneously optimized developability properties. pmc-12698359.title: Outcome comparison of lower trapezius tendon transfer and arthroscopic rotator cuff tear repair using muscle advancement for massive rotator cuff tear: a systematic review
pmc-12698359.creator: Jun Lang, Vivek Kumar Morya, Kyu-Cheol Noh
pmc-12698359.description: BackgroundThis systematic review evaluates the clinical outcomes of two distinct, arthroscopic techniques for the surgical repair of massive rotator cuff tears; lower trapezius tendon (LTT) transfer and muscle advancement (MA).MethodsEleven studies, involving 433 patients, selected based on PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) guidelines, were analyzed.

pmc-13221888.title: Interconnected Biatrial Myxoma Spanning the Fossa Ovalis
pmc-13221888.creator: Jonathan Cayo Urdiales Herrera, Heleutério da Conceição Nicolau Madogolele, Rafael Ruas Nastari, Ricardo Ribeiro Dias, Max Walter Reyes Barrenechea, Fabio Fernandes, Viviane Tiemi Hotta
pmc-13221888.description: BackgroundBiatrial myxomas are exceptionally rare; an even more unusual variant is a single tumor that straddles the interatrial septum through the fossa ovalis, forming 2 synchronous masses.Case SummaryA 74-year-old woman undergoing routine echocardiography displayed mobile lesions (3.1 × 1.4 cm left, 3.6 × 1.7 cm right) arising from a common pedicle traversing the fossa ovalis.

pmc-13556612.title: 360. Machine learning-based classification of adult attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder using cortical structural features
pmc-13556612.creator: R-A Lin, C-Y Cheng, SS-F Gau
pmc-13556612.description: BackgroundAttention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) affects a considerable proportion of adults, yet it remains frequently underdiagnosed. Machine learning approaches using brain imaging features may enhance diagnostic accuracy. Nevertheless, research focusing on adult populations, particularly in Asia, is limited.Aims & ObjectivesThis study aims to evaluate the performance of machine learning algorithms in classifying adult ADHD via analyzing regional cortical morphology.
